Quick triage update (09:36 PDT):
- What I see: concurrent-connection and kernel-scheduling latencies spiking on the pool serving gen-api; KV cache miss ratio for BrightCart routes increased ~3x at ~09:04. Tail latency correlates with cache misses and a small subset of upstream model hosts showing CPU scheduling contention.
- Immediate mitigations I recommend (order matters):
  1) Bump prefix KV TTL for BrightCart routes from 30s -> 5m (low risk, immediate) — owner: SRE (me) — ETA 10m.
  2) Enable model fallback to model-v1-small for their traffic only (reduces latency but reduces semantic fidelity) — owner: eng (Karthik) — ETA ~2-3 hours to route + test.
  3) As a short lift, request +10 dedicated capacity units from infra (if available) to reduce scheduling contention — owner: infra (I will open request) — ETA depends on capacity.
- Short-term plan: apply (1) now, evaluate impact for 15m; if insufficient, apply (2) for BrightCart only with strong monitoring for quality regressions.

Action items & owners:
- Soojin: apply TTL bump now; monitor p95 and errors.
- Karthik: prep fallback toggle (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%).
- Marissa: draft customer note for approval; don’t commit to root cause yet.

Risks: model fallback reduces answer quality; autoscale request could take time. Quantization rollouts are NOT safe for emergency roll-in without QA. Postmortem required.

Soojin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: 2027-05-23T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed latency & error rate increase — gen-api (BrightCart)

I’ll own the fallback path prep. A few technical points:
- Fallback to model-v1-small: implementation is straightforward (route variant + small shim) but decreases semantic fidelity for edge cases (recommend canary first).
- Quantization would help memory footprint and throughput long-term, but we don’t have a tested quantized variant for this model in prod — unsafe for emergency toggles.
- We can get a 5% canary out in ~45m if Soojin’s TTL bump doesn’t fully stabilize; full 100% rollout ~2-3 hours including validation. Rollback is immediate (route toggle).

Estimate: 0.75 engineer-hours to prepare canary + 1.5 engineer-hours to validate and ramp to 100% if approved.

Karthik (Eng Lead)

Sam —

Thanks again for flagging this. Brief update on actions we’ve taken and what to expect:

What we saw: an abrupt increase in p95 latency and some 5xxs for BrightCart gen-api traffic starting ~09:04 PDT.
What we did (immediate):
- Increased prefix KV TTL for BrightCart routes (30s -> 5m) to reduce repeated work; monitoring is live.
- Prepped a staged fallback to model-v1-small (lower latency) if the TTL bump does not sufficiently reduce tail latency. Karthik’s team can canary this in ~45m and fully route in 2–3 hours if needed.

Next steps:
- We’ll monitor the effect of the TTL change for 15–30m and report back. If p95 remains elevated, we’ll canary the fallback for a small portion of traffic and ramp as long as quality checks pass.
- Postmortem + root-cause analysis to follow.

We understand this hit checkout success and will follow up with a credit proposal; Laura is coordinating.

I’ll send another brief update within 90 minutes. Please reply if you want an immediate rollback or would like us to proceed with the fallback now.

Best,
